title: AI meeting assistant without human approval
prompt: Should we ship an AI meeting assistant that sends action items automatically without human approval?
whyThisCase: Product decision with competing trust and automation concerns. A strong case for structured debate if models diverge on error cost versus speed.
knownDifficulty: Models may agree superficially on “human in the loop” without naming the reversible deployment path or the minority argument for selective auto-send.
expectedFailureModes: Single-model answer flattens trade-offs into a generic caution
Side-by-side lists opinions without naming the central disagreement
Babel synthesis may over-weight consensus and under-state dissent
conciseFinding: Framework published; condition outputs and evaluation scores are not yet recorded.
whatBabelImproved: Not evaluated; no scored comparison has been recorded for this case yet.
whereBabelDidNotHelp: Until baseline and Babel runs are imported, Babel cannot be shown to help or hurt on this prompt. Expect longer completion time and higher reading burden whenever Babel is run, relative to a single-model answer.
caseConclusion: This case is published so the Lab can show a real prompt with all three evaluation conditions defined. Outputs, durations, costs, and evaluation scores remain Not recorded / Not evaluated until genuine runs are imported.
limitations: No model outputs have been recorded for any condition yet.
